byCause.title: Cannot tell whether a hidden image is decorative
byCause.detail: Whether an image left out of the accessibility tree carries information is a judgment about its content. Marlo finds the image, an `img`, an unnamed or `aria-hidden` inline `svg` or a `canvas`, and asks for a person to check; the raters found brand logos, close glyphs and a search icon whose meaning was otherwise lost.

byCause.title: Cannot tell what repeats across pages
byCause.detail: Bypass rules turn on whether a block repeats on other pages of the site, which one page cannot show. Marlo answers cantTell; the raters judged the site header repeated and found no skip link, landmark or other way past it. That includes a `main` landmark that opens with the logo link or a header holding the menu, which Marlo used to pass and now asks about.

byCause.title: Evaluates an element a stylesheet hides
byCause.detail: A button, link, field or focusable descendant is hidden by a page stylesheet: a `display:none` class on an empty edit link, a sidebar toggle with a mismatched `aria-label`, a `.hidden` link inside an `aria-hidden` region. The static renderer resolves no styles, so the rule checks something nobody can perceive. These rules read resolved `display` and `visibility` where a renderer supplies them (D-016), so in headless Chromium the element is left out and the error goes away.

byCause.title: Applies label-in-name where the raters saw abbreviations
byCause.detail: The visible labels "EN" and "Paweł Kuna UI Designer" differ from the names "Select language" and "Open user menu". The raters put both links outside the rule because the labels hold abbreviations. The pinned rule does exclude abbreviations, but its own Failed Example 1, a link showing "ACT rules" named "WCAG", treats initialisms in the label and the name as in scope, so nothing in the text separates "EN" or "UI" from them. Marlo keeps the rule as its examples apply it and reports the cell as a suspected ground-truth error rather than changing the rule toward the raters.

errors.raterA: 6 reference backlinks, e.g. a#mwAss (href #cite_ref-sec1095_1-1) and a#mwA0I: only child span.mw-linkback-text is display:none; visible 'b' comes from a CSS counter in ::before, and Chromium's a11y tree gives an empty name. Spec accname would arguably include the counter.
errors.raterB: All in-tree links have names (text, img alt, or aria-label). Six backlinks a#mwAss etc. hide their span but CSS ::before counter() supplies a letter as name.
errors.resolution: The six backlinks such as a#mwAss (href #cite_ref-sec1095_1-1) hide their span but carry ::before { content: counter(mw-ref-linkback, lower-alpha) } rendered as a visible letter (7px box). Accname step 2F.ii includes CSS generated textual content in name from content, so the name is non-empty. All other in-tree links have text, alt or aria-label names.

errors.raterA: ~1417 links in tree have names. 10 extra citation backlinks (a#mwD1I, #mwFDc, #mwFDk, #mwGeM...) show only CSS ::before counter text ('b','c'); per accname step 2F.ii that text gives a non-empty name, though Chromium computes "" for them.
errors.raterB: 10 backlink a elements, e.g. a#mwD1I href="#cite_ref-UNFPA_1-1": only content is display:none span.mw-linkback-text plus CSS counter ::before ("b"). Chromium name is empty; accname generated-content rule would give a name. All other ~1400 links named.
errors.resolution: The ten backlinks a#mwD1I, #mwD2g, #mwELE, #mwERE, #mwFDc, #mwFDk, #mwF5k, #mwGTY, #mwGTg, #mwGeM hide their span but have ::before { content: counter(mw-ref-linkback, lower-alpha) } rendered as a visible letter; accname step 2F.ii includes CSS generated text in name from content, so the name is non-empty. Every other in-tree link has a text, alt or aria-label name.
